name: George Orwell
hook: Jeopardy asks for Orwell by pen name, by real name, and by the two novels everyone knows.

facts.label: Eric Blair
facts.statement: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair — the real name Jeopardy accepts alongside Orwell.

facts.label: Nineteen Eighty-Four
facts.statement: "1984" is his 1949 dystopian novel of Big Brother and Winston Smith; it was a Cliffs Notes bestseller, and the 1984 film used Eurythmics' "Sexcrime".

facts.label: Animal Farm
facts.statement: Animal Farm is the 1945 parable subtitled "A Contemporary Satire"; its donkey Benjamin says none of the animals has ever seen a dead donkey.

facts.label: the Cold War
facts.statement: Orwell first used the term "Cold War" in print, in his 1945 essay "You and the Atomic Bomb".

facts.label: the Spanish Civil War
facts.statement: He was wounded in the Spanish Civil War fighting for the Loyalists, the experience behind Homage to Catalonia.

facts.label: Thomas Pynchon
facts.statement: Thomas Pynchon wrote that Orwell "in 1948 understood that despite the Axis defeat... fascism had not gone away".
